newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sovereign eyes manganese plant study.
newsitem.headline: Sovereign eyes manganese plant study.

text.p: Sovereign Resources (Australia) NL said on Tuesday it was proceeding with a feasibility study on a laboratory scale to produce manganese sulphate in Western Australia.

Sovereign said the decision follows a review by independent consultants indicating that production of manganese sulphate using ore from the Ant Hill deposit in Western Australia would be highly profitable.
The company said it is envisaged that a sulphate plant would be built in the iron ore port of Port Hedland to take advantage of existing infrastucture.
"Construction of a pilot plant will not be required as the process is based upon off-the-shelf technology," Sovereign said.

Capital cost of the project is estimated by Sovereign at A$7.5 million. Annual production would be around 20,000 tonnes over a 20-year mine life, generating A$12 million a year in revenues, Sovereign said.
A number of alternatives are being reviewed for funding and development of the project, Sovereign said.
Manganese sulphate is used as stock feed and fertiliser and is the primary feedstock for producing other manganese chemicals.
Ant Hill hosts a resource of 41 million tonnes of ore grading on average 25 percent manganese, Sovereign said.

Sovereign said the review is based on information provided by a number of consultants, including The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's engineering unit, Global Mining Services Pty Ltd, Dover Consultants Pty Ltd, and Micron Research.
